name: IL-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+34 open seat in deep-blue Chicago keeps the seat safely Democratic
Polymarket prices a Democratic win at about 97%
Ford out-raised Koppie more than 12-to-1; Koppie reports just $42 on hand
No general-election polls or expert ratings, so the margin size carries wide uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's D+34 lean, La Shawn Ford's dominant fundraising edge over Chad Koppie, and market pricing near 97% all point to a comfortable Democratic hold despite Danny Davis's retirement; only the size of the margin is genuinely in question.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Ford or the arrival of actual general-election polling could shift the expected margin, though it is unlikely to threaten the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Danny Davis (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Illinois's 7th District is one of the most Democratic seats in the country, and Danny Davis's retirement leaves state Rep. La Shawn Ford as the Democratic nominee. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised more than $720,000, while Republican Chad Koppie has raised under $60,000 and reports just $42 on hand.

Prediction markets put the Democratic chance near 97%, and no general-election polls exist to challenge the district's strong Democratic lean. Roughly $2.5 million in outside spending opposing Ford is the only notable wrinkle, but in a seat this heavily Democratic the realistic question is the size of the winning margin, not which party holds the seat.
